chapter: Later career and The Benny Goodman Story
title: The Benny Goodman Story: Steve Allen, Sol Yaged and the soundtrack
summary: Wilson explains that the music was recorded first and Allen mimed to it with Yaged coaching; Wilson played piano on the whole track though Jess Stacey was Goodman's big-band pianist.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: We were talking about when you went out to California to do the picture, The Benny Goodman Story. Now there should be some interesting things to tell about that. Let's see, Sol Yaged was teaching somebody to play Benny ...

That's right, Steve Allen played the role of Benny Goodman, and Sol coached Steve Allen on synchronizing the camera shots with the sound track. See, they recorded the whole sound track -- the music was all recorded first, and then the camera work was done later with the sound track being blasted over loud speakers for the musicians to hear and memorize the improvisations as they go over it again and again, until they finally got a pretty good synchronization of sound and sight.

So it was recorded first, because Goodman recorded all the clarinet on the sound track, but Steve Allen was photographed doing it all, and Sol was his coach and taught him how to hold the clarinet and to make it appear plausible that he was actually playing the clarinet when he wasn't.

And in regard to the piano, I did the whole piano sound track, but the truth of the matter, Jess Stacey should have been on the big banders, the big band tracks, because in real life, I only played with the trio and and quartet. Jess Stacey was the big band player with Goodman.

He was with the band when I joined it in the Congress Hotel in Chicago -- I joined to play only with the trio, and then later, of course the quartet with Lionel -- and even after I left, Stacey was still the big band player with Goodman.

But for some reason or another, Stacey and Goodman didn't get together, I think on the business part of it, because I do recall Stacey walking out of the studio after a meeting one day, and then Goodman asking me to do the big band recording, as well as the small groups.
